CASE FILE — Concepcion v. United States
Docket: 20-1650 | Term: OT2021 | Court below: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
Parties: Carlos Concepcionv. United States of America (Petitioner v. Respondent)
Question presented: Must or may a district court consider intervening legal and factual developments when deciding whether to “impose a reduced sentence” on an individual under Section 404(b) of the First Step Act of 2018?
Facts: In 2008, Carlos Concepcion pleaded guilty to crack cocaine charges, and in 2009 he was sentenced to 228 months in prison. While he was serving his sentence, Congress passed the Fair Sentencing Act, which reduced the statutory penalties for most federal crimes involving crack cocaine. In 2018, Congress made these changes retroactive, and Concepcion moved for resentencing. The district court denied his motion, and Concepcion appealed. The U.S. Court of Appeals affirmed, finding that the district court was not obligated to update and reevaluate the sentencing factors.
Posture: Writ of certiorari
